Subject: Intro demo on 2/16 — thoughts on switching to product-integration scoping

Hi Olivia —

Thanks again for taking time to chat last week. I wanted to follow up on the intro demo we had penciled for Feb 16 and propose switching the session format to a targeted product-integration scoping workshop instead. From our side that would be a 90-minute working session (10–15 minute context, 60–65 minute technical scoping, 10–15 minute next steps) focused on:

- integration touchpoints (APIs/batches/webhooks)
- data residency and retention constraints
- performance/throughput targets for near-term MVP

I heard that your engineering lead will be traveling that week — if that’s still the case, we can either move the workshop to a different date or run a condensed technical deep dive with your product manager and tech lead on the line.

Proposed workshop slots (PT):
- Tue Feb 16, 10:00–11:30 PT
- Wed Feb 17, 08:30–10:00 PT (backup)

If you prefer to keep it as a high-level intro demo, that’s totally fine — I just want to make sure we bring the right folks and prep the right materials so the meeting is productive.

Do either of the slots above work? Also can you confirm the attendee list (roles) and any network/whitelist constraints ahead of time?

Thanks —
Logan Wright
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

- Tue Feb 16, 10:00–11:30 PT — PM + integration engineer attend; tech lead absent
- Thu Feb 18, 09:00–10:30 PT — PM + tech lead available

Olivia —

We can definitely run the 90-minute scoping workshop with the option to scale back if the tech lead can’t join. Karthik (cc’d) will lead the technical session. I’ve drafted a proposed agenda and a short checklist for the MVP integration (attached) — highlights:

Agenda (90 min):
- 0–10m: context, goals, success criteria (Olivia / FinSecure PM)
- 10–30m: architecture overview & data flow (FinSecure)
- 30–80m: technical scoping (Redwood solutions + FinSecure engineers)
  - API contract review
  - auth & network requirements
  - expected throughput & SLOs
- 80–90m: next steps & owners (mutual action plan)

Can you confirm who from FinSecure will present the architecture (diagram or brief slide)? Also please send any pre-reads you want us to review — Karthik asked for the endpoint inventory and any sample payloads.

Proposed confirmed slot: Tue Feb 16, 10:00–11:30 PT (we’ll hold that and switch to Feb 18 if Maya confirms travel conflict).

I’m attaching: product_integration_agenda.pdf and MVP-integration-checklist.xlsx — please review and send any additions. Logan, Marissa — can you coordinate the calendar invite and breakout rooms (Zoom + breakout for API vs infra)?

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com

Attachments: product_integration_agenda.pdf, MVP-integration-checklist.xlsx

Thanks team — quick technical notes:

1) API versions: do you expect to be on v1.2 or the upcoming v2 preview in Q1? If v2 preview, we should allocate extra time to discuss differences (auth flow and rate limits).
2) Pre-reads we need: endpoint inventory (CSV ok), sample payloads for typical requests, and any network egress IPs or proxy details.
3) Performance targets: please indicate concurrent request targets and typical payload sizes (50–95th percentile). That will determine whether we recommend a streaming vs batched integration pattern.

If Maya (tech lead) is out Feb 15–17, I’m fine to run the session on Feb 16 with your integrations engineer and the PM. But if there are open questions that require Maya’s approvals (e.g., KMS/HSM choices, VPC peering), we should plan a short follow-up on Feb 18 when she’s back.

Proposed backup: Wed Feb 17, 08:30–10:00 PT or Thu Feb 18, 09:00–10:30 PT (final backup if deeper approvals required).

I’ll prepare a short runbook and split the technical scoping into two parallel threads (API contract + infra/network) so we can run breakouts if needed.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
